hook: A Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W runs a tiny transformer that plays games.
hooks: A Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W runs a tiny transformer that plays games.
It uses two tiny neural nets to generate frames and choose actions.
SheepSeb says the world model uses 26k–131k parameters.
what_happened: A looped transformer and a small MLP run on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, generating game frames and selecting actions in real time.
try_it: Run a game with `uv run python -m tinyworldformer.games.play --game pacman`.
why_it_matters: It lets a microcontroller both imagine and play simple games without external hardware.
the_catch: Exact‑frame accuracy excludes frames right after random events, which cannot be predicted.
caption: A tiny looped transformer can generate and play games directly on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. Can your microcontroller dream up games?
alt_text: The slides explain that a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W runs a tiny looped transformer that creates and plays simple games, its performance numbers, and its current limitation.
